findings.claim: The candidate omits the publication date, a factual metadata value covered by the preservation requirement. This is a deterministic omission regardless of whether the site can infer a date elsewhere.
findings.suggestion: Restore `date: 2025-05-31` without changing `modified`.

findings.quote: Cada generación descubre su propio espantajo tecnológico. Surge un nuevo dispositivo y, de repente, la civilización tamborilea al borde de la idiocia. Podrías poner tu Apple Watch en hora con estos pánicos —suponiendo que tenga batería. No sea que tengamos que recurrir a la relojería analógica.
findings.sourceQuote: Every generation discovers its technological bogeyman. Some new device emerges, and suddenly civilization teeters on the brink of idiocy. You could set your Apple Watch by these panics—assuming it has a charge. Lest we resort to analog timekeeping.
findings.claim: “Tamborilea” means drums or taps, so it does not convey civilization teetering. “Relojería analógica” also evokes a craft or industry rather than the simple act of checking a clock. Together they turn deliberate dry humor into accidental awkwardness. The parenthetical dash is also left unclosed.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite the opening: “Cada generación encuentra una nueva amenaza tecnológica. Aparece un dispositivo y ya parece que la civilización está a un paso de volverse idiota. Estos ataques de pánico son tan puntuales que podrías poner en hora tu Apple Watch con ellos. Si tiene batería, claro. No vaya a tocar mirar un reloj analógico.” This preserves recurrent panic, threatened intelligence, and the battery joke. It gives up the bogeyman image and the English sentence pattern to gain natural pacing and a clear punchline.

findings.quote: revisemos nuestros recibos históricos
findings.sourceQuote: let's check our historical receipts
findings.claim: “Recibos históricos” suggests old payment receipts without making the intended meaning—checking the record—clear. The source's colloquial challenge becomes an unexplained English calque.
findings.suggestion: Use “repasemos el historial de estos pánicos”. This retains the invitation to examine prior evidence and its skeptical attitude. It loses the receipt metaphor but gains immediate comprehension and a direct transition into the historical examples.

findings.quote: ¿Quién se rasga ahora las manos por la pérdida de las habilidades de lectura de mapas?
findings.sourceQuote: Who is hand-wringing about the loss of map-reading skills now?
findings.claim: “Rasgarse las manos” is not the intended expression of anxious lament; it introduces an image of tearing one's hands. This undermines a key rhetorical question and makes the writer sound unfamiliar with Spanish idiom.
findings.suggestion: Use “¿Quién se lamenta ahora de que ya no sepamos leer mapas?” The adaptation preserves dismissive impatience and the question-answer rhythm. It drops the physical gesture and gains an idiomatic formulation readable across regions.

findings.quote: **Los estudiantes necesitan entender** cuándo la IA amplifica el aprendizaje frente a cuando lo corta en seco.
findings.sourceQuote: **Students need to understand** when AI amplifies learning versus short-circuits development.
findings.claim: “Lo” refers to “el aprendizaje”, removing the explicit distinction between helping learning and bypassing or impeding development. “Corta en seco” additionally presents an abrupt halt rather than the source's short-circuit metaphor. This alters the article's central educational recommendation.
findings.suggestion: Use “**Los estudiantes necesitan entender** cuándo la IA potencia el aprendizaje y cuándo interfiere en su desarrollo.” This restores development as the second concept. It trades the electrical metaphor for a clear statement of the educational risk.

findings.quote: El reto no es impedir su uso, sino **enseñar su aplicación efectiva**, construyendo alfabetización en torno a ella.
findings.sourceQuote: The challenge isn't preventing its use but **teaching its effective application**, building literacy around it.
findings.claim: “Construyendo alfabetización en torno a ella” is an awkward abstract calque. Combined with “enseñar su aplicación efectiva”, it gives the main recommendation an institutional tone that weakens the source's directness.
findings.suggestion: Use “El reto no es impedir su uso, sino **enseñar a usarla bien** y desarrollar los conocimientos necesarios para hacerlo.” This preserves effective use and literacy while replacing abstract noun phrases with ordinary verbs. The compact literacy label is lost; clarity and the author's direct voice are gained.

findings.quote: **Los educadores deben rediseñar las evaluaciones** para un mundo aumentado por la IA.
findings.sourceQuote: **Educators must redesign assessments** for an AI-augmented world.
findings.claim: “Un mundo aumentado” is understandable but reads as a literal import; it does not express the idea of AI extending human capabilities as naturally as the surrounding argument requires.
findings.suggestion: Consider “**Los educadores deben rediseñar las evaluaciones** para un mundo en el que la IA amplía nuestras capacidades.” This makes the augmentation relationship explicit without adding a separate factual claim.

findings.quote:
title: "Los Últimos en Pensar"
subTitle: ¿Humano o Máquina?
findings.sourceQuote:
title: "The Last to Think"
subTitle: Human or Machine?
findings.claim: The internal capitalization follows English title case rather than ordinary Spanish title conventions. The plural interpretation of “The Last” is defensible and is not itself a defect.
findings.suggestion: Use `title: "Los últimos en pensar"` and `subTitle: ¿Humano o máquina?`.

sourceConcerns: “In the 1940s, educators warned that CliffsNotes would make students lazy readers.” The CliffsNotes chronology requires historical verification. The supplied checked packet contains no relevant historical reference, so this review does not assert a corrected date. The candidate inherits the claim; a translator should not silently repair it.

“Most people under 40 can't read paper maps.” This quantitative population claim has no supporting evidence in the supplied packet. “La mayoría de las personas menores de 40 años” preserves it accurately; any substantiation or qualification belongs in a source revision.

“No, it can't replicate human emotional intelligence or creativity.” The source states a categorical capability limit without defining replication or supporting the distinction. “No, no puede replicar la inteligencia emocional ni la creatividad humanas” faithfully carries that limitation; it is not a translation-introduced error.

“crutches that will hobble a generation.” The source presents this wording as a historical quotation without attribution in the supplied materials. Verify the quotation at source level before treating it as documented historical evidence.
